column1: # Specified by The Designer, Step 1 Wave 2 review section 3.3; accepted by The Manager at the
# Step 1 close, decision 5.2. Built and loaded at sub-step 1.14 by The Engineer.
# quantity-id is written BARE, without brackets, so tools/quantities.js does not read this
# column as a quotation tag. oracle/** is inside the counting rule's declared file set.
#   AM-1 no two rows with state:owed name the same non-"-" quantity id
#   AM-2 every superseded-by resolves to a row that is not itself superseded
#   AM-3 every target is a row in oracle/MANIFEST.tsv
#   AM-4 no row is applied while its target's manifest row reads specified

column9: ABORT is defined twice and the two definitions contradict. BLOCKING.
partially-acquired turns on an undefined word and contradicts dirty-or-diverged. BLOCKING.
missing-recoverable is unassignable and the blocking-set partition counts it anyway. BLOCKING.
Node absent gives CLEAN and BC-4 has no consumer. BLOCKING.
The marker rule is not applied completely; the falsifier column says where. MAJOR.

BC-8 passes against a hooks directory that does not exist; remedy was assert the directory holds a file. DECLINED by 1.13 section 3.1: a directory holding pre-commit.sh, or pre-commit at mode 100644, satisfies that form and fires nothing. The finding is taken, the remedy is not.
The bootstrap does not detect a fresh clone missing the corpus data files. Add BC-20. MAJOR. Close condition is a date; X2 makes it the Step 1 gate grep.
BC-1's command cannot falsify BC-1's falsifier. MAJOR.
Idempotence is asserted, not assertable, on three counts, one measured. MAJOR.
BC-5 measures the working directory, not the root, and does not enforce its own clause. MINOR.
BC-7's self-deletion clause cannot fire, which makes the clause permanent by accident. MINOR.
BC-14 asserts one of the four markers its own justification names. MINOR.
BC-19 is a fact sitting in a table of assertions; reclassify as fact 3 of the install state record. MINOR.
Section 6's LITERATURE availability is narrower than the answer contract at version 2. MINOR. Depends on AM-66.

The simplicity gate takes the assertion count 19 to 15. SUPERSEDED AT R-2 into AM-24, which is the same edit: AM-15 moved the value and AM-24 minted the block at the value AM-15 leaves, so neither can land without the other. AM-1 reported them as a collision because it cannot see that two rows are one edit. They are now one row. Nothing about the content is withdrawn.
Delete ABORT's second sentence; the outcome line carries ABORT (<phase>, <assertion-id>). 1.5's application of F1.
Define usable: present, and in neither offline nor present-but-wrong. 1.5's application of F2.
Demote missing-recoverable to a Phase 3 transient; it leaves the mode table. 1.5's application of F3.
Q-DEGRADED-MODES 6 to 5, with a superseded entry.
Q-BLOCKING-MODES predicate 3-of-6 to 3-of-5, population 5 rows, with a superseded entry. Its population cell names Q-DEGRADED-MODES, so this lands in the same edit as AM-19.

Assert the hook file exists, is non-empty, begins with #! and carries the marker naming its check register row. OVERRULED at the 1.5/1.13 review X1 in favour of AM-33, which argues explicitly against this form. CLOSED AT R-2: the marker clause landed as CL-8(b) of oracle/check_register.md (every row whose path is under tools/githooks/ contains the literal CHK- id of its own row), and cr_scratch/step1_5_systems_engineer_install_state.md section 3.1 row 5 now carries the OVERRULED marker inline, so a reader applying that list no longer applies a rejected amendment.
Measure $ROOT in the shell, not pwd in Node; the long-name clause moves to Phase 1's binding of $ROOT. 1.5's application of F4 and F10.

The reviewer's own list, accepted without restatement and landing in the same edit: BC-4 wired into section 6's origin table; BC-13 merged into BC-12 with two markers; BC-14 asserting all four markers; BC-16 deferred to the sub-step writing the divergence check; BC-3 and BC-15 cut; section 6's LITERATURE and CONTESTED availability conditions split; BC-9's remedy guarded with a --get; the idempotence definition qualified with "and an unchanged upstream"; idempotent replaced by unconditional for Phases 1-6.

One edit, absorbing AM-15. Take the bootstrap contract's assertion count from 19 to 15 per the 1.4 simplicity gate, AND mint Q-BOOTSTRAP-ASSERTIONS at the value that edit leaves. The quantity is stated in two files today with no block, so it is governed by test G1 until this lands. It was deliberately not minted at 1.5 because the value moves in the same week.

Section 1's bare phrase "the four facts" is a second site for Q-STATE-FACTS and comes into <value> [<id>] form under the Tier 2 touch rule. SUPERSEDED AT R-2 into AM-39. Counting rule section 4 step 4 already requires that every site the checker lists is updated in the SAME edit as the value, so this was never a separate amendment; filed as one, it produced exactly the failure 1.14 predicted -- land them apart and the bootstrap contract ships 4 [Q-STATE-FACTS] against a block reading 3.
Replace the five-value verdict table with the two axes of currency policy section 6, with the stated token mapping and three new tokens: withdrawn, behind, diverged.

The direction discriminator is defined only where CURRENCY is upstream-ahead; exit 128 is unknown rather than false. --is-ancestor is reflexive and unguarded accuses the author on every equal session.
git -C <copy> fetch --quiet --prune origin. Without --prune a branch deleted upstream keeps resolving. Measured.
V is the ref of the last row for that copy in oracle/VERIFIED.tsv, which is now append-only.

The idempotence definition's "the timestamp" becomes "written_at and every observed_at" - there are four, and a 6.1 fixture written against the singular reads three violations against a correct implementation.
State idempotence over the right pair of runs: run N+1 is identical to run N in every field but the timestamps, and in every report line, whenever run N wrote no new value to copies. Closes F9b.
Add: never git pull in a working copy. pull is a fetch with a merge attached and the merge is the prohibited half.

Delete BC-8 as written. Replace with: git config core.hooksPath tools/githooks then node tools/checks.js --wiring, running HK-1 and HK-2 of the check register. Every register row naming pre-commit is reported UNWIRED by id on failure. WINS X1 over AM-21.
oracle/VERIFIED.tsv becomes append-only, five columns, # rows=<n>. Seeded content at currency policy section 3.
copies.lsei.head's reader widens to: the next run's Phase 5; the answering loop, as a comparand. The wrongness cell widens and does not weaken.

The consumer count is unchanged at 4. The answering loop already appears; it now reads two fields rather than one. No new consumer, no block correction. Recorded because a reader of the widened section 5 will expect the count to move.

Section 6.1 validated before it branched, so a future record that adds a key was classified corrupt and rewritten by 6.3, destroying what 6.4 exists to protect. BLOCKING. APPLIED AT R-2: section 4 is split into 4a the parse gate (rules 1-3, true at every schema version) and 4b the shape gate (rules 4-6, true only at this version); 6.1 becomes open, 4a, schema-greater, schema-less, 4b, ordinary, with the two orderings named as non-exchangeable. Section 3's future-version fixture becomes two, F1 (schema 2, same paths) and F2 (schema 2 plus one added key); F2 is the case the single published fixture could not reach, and 6.4's falsifier list now names it.
Rule 4 contradicts the write-whole-or-not-at-all rule and the self-check fixture cannot see it. BLOCKING.

Delete pdfs_present: it manufactures the failure it is meant to avoid. Takes Q-STATE-FACTS 4 to 3. MAJOR. Absorbs AM-25 at R-2: the SAME edit brings oracle/bootstrap_contract.md section 1's bare phrase "the four facts" into <value> [<id>] form at the new value. AM-40 rides the same edit for Q-STATE-KEYS 19 to 18. Landing any of the three alone is the defect.
The same edit as AM-39 takes Q-STATE-KEYS 19 to 18.
Section 7's rename guarantee is false under a concurrent reader, and section 7 has no wrongness column. MAJOR.
M1 is not decidable as written: it refuses corpus.digest. MAJOR.
M3 has two readings and the second admits what the first refuses. MAJOR.
written_at's stated reason is false on the file's own text. MINOR.
The keystone holds only on a run that reaches both upstreams, and section 6.2 misreports a deletion. MINOR.
Add CHK-25 (oracle/lib/verify_app_ref.js) and CHK-26 (tools/check_verified_tsv.js), both specified.
CHK-23's asserts and authority cells widen.

Q-CHECK-ROWS 24 to 26 and specified 15 to 17, with the H row written as the literal H 1 <date> 26 7 17 2. SUPERSEDED AT R-2 by AM-108: under the reclassification no amendment states this integer at all, so AM-46's rows can land without anyone forecasting a checksum. The row additions AM-48 was paired with are AM-46's and stay owed.

CHK-09 asserting HK-1 under CHK-10 dispatch is unbounded recursion. BLOCKING. APPLIED AT R-2: CHK-09 becomes --register (CL-1 to CL-8, pre-commit and session-start, block) and the new CHK-29 becomes --wiring (HK-1 and HK-2, session-start only, report). Section 5.1 of the check register records the loop, the measurement, and why the environment-sentinel alternative was refused. The sentinel makes an assertion's meaning depend on its caller, which is the ambiguity R5 is about.

The consolidation survivor ecr_verify.js could not lift a marked block from a CRLF file, and the silent check produced a wrong verification. The CRLF-tolerant lifter is committed and The Manager verified it at the close. The remaining halves - its absolute require path and the check that cannot fail - are AM-51.

The remaining half of R2 after AM-50 and AM-107: tools/ecr_verify.js resolves its require() of the upstream tokenizer through a hard-coded absolute ROOT, so the consolidation at 2.15 must RE-DERIVE that require rather than lift it, or it lifts the portability defect into the survivor. Owed to 2.15. The wiring half is AM-107 and landed at R-2.
CL-5(b) is not an expiry; it is a permanent exemption with a name on it. MAJOR.

Four rows carried an invocation in the path cell. APPLIED AT R-2: CHK-14 to CHK-17 all carry path tools/quantities.js and the mode moves to a literal prefix on asserts (--check:, --lint:, --index:, --live:), on the marker: <literal> precedent, no tenth column. CL-3 gains the clause that would have caught it on day one: path contains no whitespace. CHK-27 and CHK-28 are written in the same form.

CHK-09 had two invokers wanting two consequences, which its own boundary rule forbids: block at pre-commit, report at session-start per 1.13 section 3.2. APPLIED AT R-2 in the same edit as AM-49: the --register / --wiring split gives each consequence its own row, and CHK-29 is report.
CL-6's marker is an English phrase, and CHK-20 is where to set the precedent. MINOR.
CL-6's remedy makes four checks depend on a gitignored working copy, and one of them is on pre-commit. MINOR.
HK-2 asserts the mode bit; nothing asserts the line endings, and the repository commits CR bytes. Commit .gitattributes with tools/githooks/* text eol=lf before installing hooks. MINOR.
Add CL-7(b): an exec-reviewed:<substep> token in authority, so a new row that executes harvested strings and is honestly kinded check has a blocking guard. Uses CL-5's existing device, no new column.

Add CL-8. APPLIED AT R-2 with two clauses: (a) no row whose invoked_by names pre-commit contains the literal "git hook run pre-commit" -- an assertion may not invoke the event it asserts; (b) every row whose path is under tools/githooks/ contains the literal CHK- id of its own row, which is the marker clause relocated from AM-21 and makes CHK-10's dispatch join bidirectional. Both verified green against the amended register.
Splitting CHK-09 adds one row. APPLIED AT R-2 with AM-49. The competition this row was filed to make visible is closed by AM-108, not by this row winning it.

tools/quantities.js needs a row, adding one more. APPLIED AT R-2: it had four already; AM-53 made them joinable and AM-103 made them live. The added rows at R-2 are CHK-27, CHK-28 and CHK-29. Closed by AM-108, not by this row winning.

CONTESTED cannot buy two personas: a register axis may carry any number of sides and truncating to two makes the router choose which sides the user hears. APPLIED AT R-3 as part of the single version-2 edit. Contract section 1: one per side, minimum two, no cap. Suite VRD-7 amended, VRD-9 generalized from a pair to a set. The quantity cell named Q-LCC-SIDES-GT2 (10 of 15 on the Step 0 draft); the warrant that survives is Q-LCC15-SIDES-GT2 (7 of 15 on the authored rows), whose own conditions field reconciles the two. No numeral is carried into the contract: the contract states the rule and the measurement stays in its birth file.

A one_sided axis cannot produce a CONTESTED verdict. APPLIED AT R-3 in the version-2 edit. Contract section 1: CONTESTED fires on class two_sided or false_pair; one_sided produces LITERATURE or BOTH carrying its side and the one-side disclosure at register_schema section 7. Suite VRD-13, LIM-10 and LIM-11 added. The failure it prevents is an unsatisfiable requirement, which fails as a refusal carrying no reason code.

Rule V CONTESTED moves findings from Forbidden to permitted-and-never-counted. APPLIED AT R-3 in the version-2 edit. Rule V gains a FOURTH COLUMN, Permitted-not-counted, because a two-column parser finds findings in neither column, emits the version-1 cell list against the version-2 rules, and returns green. Suite RV-25 flips to legal, RV-35 and RV-36 added, RV-34 retired and replaced by RV-37 which asserts 35 cells and 10 legal.

The misclassified reason code condition is container-shaped and is replaced. APPLIED AT R-3 in the version-2 edit. Contract section 5: fires on any nonzero match_keys overlap with an axis the returned file belongs to, while classification did not fire that axis at its stated firing rule. Owner unchanged and still match_keys. Suite REF-7 and REF-11 amended, REF-18 added as the false-refusal defence.

Contract version 1 becomes 2. APPLIED AT R-3. The file read 1 while nine other files read 2. Landed as ONE edit carrying eleven amendments, per the amended section 9: the integer names a state of the file, not a count of the amendments that produced it. AM-73 is superseded by this row rather than adding a third bump.

Every trace line whose origin is app names the lsei ref the value was computed against. APPLIED AT R-3 in the version-2 edit. Arity unchanged; the ref rides the locator and the origin function strips it before resolving. Suite TRC-12 added, with a decoy: strip the ref from one app trace and TRC-12 goes red while TRC-3 stays green, because a fixed-arity parser cannot see it.
The ref is read live once per run, git -C lsei rev-parse --short HEAD, never from .oracle-state.json. APPLIED AT R-3 in the version-2 edit, contract section 3.

The live ref is compared against copies.lsei.head; a mismatch is a report line on the answer. APPLIED AT R-3 in the version-2 edit, contract section 3. Stated as a report and NOT a refusal, because the working copy moving mid-session is the drafting assumption A3 doing what it assumes, and a refusal there refuses a working install.

Every run log row records the app ref, or - where lsei was absent. APPLIED AT R-3 in the version-2 edit. Nine fields, closed. Suite LOG-12 amended from eight to nine and LOG-25 added. The column is not recoverable from the traces: a run that emitted no app trace records the ref anyway, and finding every answer computed before lsei moved is one grep over the log against a parse of every deliverable file on disk.

An app trace with no ref is a refusal, reason code input-missing, owner the bootstrap. APPLIED AT R-3 in the version-2 edit, WITH ITS TIMING PINNED, which is the whole content of the change. The refusal fires at the START of the run, when the ref cannot be read, before classification and with zero personas spent. A refusal reached after the wave has run costs more than the answer it replaces and breaks section 5 unconditional zero-persona rule. An app trace missing its ref after a successful read is an emitter defect, not a refusal. Suite REF-20.

DECLINED AT R-3, and the reason is that this row is filed against the wrong target. The finding (1.4-review F14) is that oracle/bootstrap_contract.md section 6 states one availability condition for two verdicts that have different ones. The answer contract Rule V already distinguishes them and always did: LITERATURE requires at least one literature OR findings, CONTESTED requires one literature per side and permits findings without counting it. There is no contract-side change owed. The whole fix is AM-14 on the bootstrap contract. A pair-row written on both sides of a one-sided finding is a defect of this register, not of the contract.

The run-log schema extension is a third bump, to version 3. SUPERSEDED BY AM-66 AT R-3. It is a real CHANGE and not a real BUMP: the extension landed as AM-70 inside the single version-2 edit. The version integer names a state of the file, not a count of the changes that produced it, and section 9 now says so in the rule rather than in a note. This row is the artefact of the ambiguity, and it is the cleanest evidence that the ambiguity was in the rule and not in either author.

DECLINED AT R-3. Minting a quantity id for the contract version integer is the wrong instrument, and the reason is a property of the quantity rather than of the effort. The counting rule class fixed asserts ONE current value and requires every site to agree; live means a value that moves on its own. The version integer is neither: each file legitimately states the version IT was written against, so a Step 0 document reading 1 is correct and would be made wrong by a tag. The two consumers that matter already have a stronger mechanism than the counting rule - VER-1/2/3 and LOG-20 assert agreement at run time and fail when it breaks, which is how this collision surfaced at all. AM-1 blindness is closed by AM-112 instead, which groups owed rows on (target, section) and needs no id.

Q-ROOT-ALLOWANCE names derived-from: Q-PATH-CEILING-259 and no such block exists. M4 reports it as a dangling parent today. Mint the block from the bisection at 1.7 section 8: 259 pass, 260 fail, git 2.55.0.windows.1, core.longpaths unset at all three scopes, OS LongPathsEnabled 0.

Q-ROOT-ALLOWANCE rests on two parents, not one. The second is 108, which is chosen rather than measured (10 + 1 + 32 + 1 + 64) and has no id. Mint it, and add it to derived-from, or the staleness graph cannot see the input most likely to be revisited.

literature/FIELDS.tsv and literature/INDEX.tsv re-admission. The .gitignore half is applied; the NAMING.md half states that the two literals are the corpus's machine-readable files and that a future .tsv is a decision rather than a side effect.
Duplicate id: the block exists in both step1_9 and its addendum. Move, do not copy - COUNTING_RULE.md section 8 permits a block to move between files and does not permit one to exist in two.
Duplicate id, and the two blocks disagree: 58 in step1_9, 59 in the addendum. M3 fails as well as M2.
Duplicate id. Named nowhere before Wave 2.

The worked example cannot be lifted without failing four of its own checks. Add an example namespace: an id beginning Q-EG- is an example, may not be minted as a real block, and is skipped by M2, M3 and M4; and a quantity fence nested inside a four-backtick fence is not a block. HARD. APPLIED AT R-4. Q-EG- example namespace and the nested-fence rule are in section 2; the worked example is rewritten in that namespace; the real Q-PAIR-IDENTICAL and Q-OVERLAP-95 blocks are minted in cr_scratch/step1_r4_designer_counting_rule_v2.md section 2, both re-measured rather than copied forward.

Section 5 promises a lint that section 7 never mechanizes: a bare governed numeral in a second file. Either specify M13 or delete the row from section 5. tools/quantities.js --lint implements a candidate M13 at 1.14; the contract still has to choose. HARD. APPLIED AT R-4. M13 is specified in section 9 and the section 5 row is KEPT. Ruling in the R-4 report section 5: deleting the row would have made a governed integer with three competing successors permanently invisible. M13 reports 13 findings today.

M11 is weaker than the rule it implements and fails on exactly the two blocks that needed it (Q-HOOKSPATH-INERT, Q-REG-TSV-IGNORED). M11 becomes: conditions matches cwd: followed, before the next sentence break, by \d+ characters. Implemented behind --w2-3 at 1.14. HARD. APPLIED AT R-4. Section 2 requires cwd: <description>, <n> characters and section 9 M11 checks it. Both blocks W2-3 predicted fired; one was fixed by its own author mid-pass, the other is AM-130.

operation admits three forms and none is arithmetic over other quantities, which derived-from presupposes. Add a fourth form, derived: <expression over ids>, and have M4 evaluate it. HARD. APPLIED AT R-4. The derived: <expression over ids> form is section 2 and M4 evaluates it against the parents values. First real use is AM-128.

derived-from's rule becomes: every input to the value, measured or chosen, carries an id. The instance is AM-76. MAJOR. APPLIED AT R-4. Section 2 derived-from now reads: every input to the value carries an id, measured or chosen. Its limit is named in AM-131.

Section 4's four-part correction has no form for a correction whose sites are in a document another persona has frozen. Add a pending: entry naming the target document and the amendment id in this register. MAJOR. This register is the other half. APPLIED AT R-4. pending: <target> - <AM-id> in the superseded field, section 4, checked by M4 against this register. A pending: naming no row here is a hard failure.

Two ids for one quantity and nothing detects it: Q-C4-SOURCE-LEN and Q-C4-SOURCE-LINES are the same 328-line measurement. Delete Q-C4-SOURCE-LEN from 1.12 section 6 and quote Q-C4-SOURCE-LINES. MAJOR. APPLIED AT R-4, ruled HUMAN with a machine hint. M14 reports two blocks sharing a unit or a population; H8 rules whether they are one quantity. M14 finds 2 candidates today, both of which H8 would clear, which is the argument for it being a lint. Q-C4-SOURCE-LEN is deleted from 1.12 section 6 and now quotes Q-C4-SOURCE-LINES.

No form for quoting a range, so M3 cannot read one. 357-686 inclusive [Q-C4-FENCE-SPAN] gives M3 the token "inclusive". MAJOR. 1.14 measures 47 further unreadable-token sites; see the report. APPLIED AT R-4, both halves. Section 3 rules 8 and 9 state the adjacency and range forms; M3 also became a tolerant reader. Isolated on one tree: strict 46 unreadable sites, tolerant 36. All ten recovered were markup; all 36 remaining have a noun before the tag and need author edits.

1.6 section 3.5 asked for a clause and it is not in the contract: a file declaring its own size is not a quotation of it. Covers oracle/VERIFIED.tsv's # rows=5, the loose-ends register's 44 rows, the check register's H row, and now MANIFEST.tsv and this file. MAJOR. APPLIED AT R-4 as section 3 rule 10, deliberately narrow: a header or trailer whose subject is the file it sits in. Covers oracle/VERIFIED.tsv, the loose-ends register, and the H rows of MANIFEST.tsv and this file. Also closes AM-109(a).

The contract states "the nine instances" at five sites and scores itself against nine; step1_author_rulings.md records a tenth three minutes earlier. Run instance 10 against the contract. MINOR. APPLIED AT R-4. Instance 10 re-measured - 19-file shelf, 14 generic names, both reproduce - and scored in the R-4 report section 8. Verdict PARTIAL, and it is an arm-2 instance rather than an arm-1 one: reached only by section 3 rule 12 and H7. The 1.12 scorecard stands at nine and is not amended.

Two directory-map rows for literature/FIELDS.tsv and literature/INDEX.tsv, added FIRST. Ordering is load-bearing: CHK-12 then fails until the .gitignore re-admission lands, which forces the second half instead of relying on memory.
Re-admit literature/FIELDS.tsv and literature/INDEX.tsv as named literals. Verified at 1.14 by git check-ignore: both tracked; the control probe literature/NAMING.tsv is correctly ignored.

Duplicate id across step1_10 and its addendum, and the two disagree: 17 against 18. R-6 landed the addendum after the Wave 2 review ran, so this is W2-11's shape repeated in 1.10 and named nowhere. Four siblings follow.
Duplicate id across step1_10 and its addendum.

Duplicate id across step1_10 and its addendum.

Two H rows, one file. RULED AND APPLIED AT R-2 by The Systems Engineer; The Engineer declined it correctly at 1.14 as a schema question rather than a promotion question. THE MERGE IS REFUSED. oracle/register_schema.md gains section 3.0: the sidecar is a SET of files, oracle/REGISTER.<corpus>.tsv, one basis_root each, joined at load. basis_root, basis_date and basis_ref bind the whole file; a merged file could carry two corpora only by moving basis_root onto every A row, at which point L4 has no root to name in its failure message. Three clauses: SET-1 one root per file, SET-2 axis ids unique across the loaded set, SET-3 each file validated in full against its own root and the loader's output is the union. Section 9 gains L0 (header cardinality) and L1b (set uniqueness). The manifest row for oracle/REGISTER.tsv is state:superseded so the path resolves to the ruling.

tools/ecr_verify.js read the H row as last-H-wins with no cardinality check, so against a two-H file it silently validated the SECOND header. The SCHEMA half was ruled at R-2 as register_schema section 9 L0. The CODE half is APPLIED AT R-3: ecr_verify.js now fails on a second H row and on an H row that is not the first non-comment row. Measured on the same concatenation of the two promoted halves: the run reports L0 row 98 is a second H row, and its L2 lines now report the FIRST header counts 15/81 where they previously reported the second header 18/53. Both promoted registers still exit 0.

step1_10 and step1_10_addendum carry the SAME marker name, "oracle/REGISTER.tsv (ECR rows)". 1.9's author named the addendum marker distinctly for exactly this reason. A sed naming that marker is ambiguous across files, and the addendum's own section 5 command uses a truncated pattern that matches either. MANIFEST.tsv's MF-3 join is keyed on (source-file, marker) at 1.14 to work around it.

Four deliverables state a lift command with no sed '1d;$d', so the promoted file would begin with its own BEGIN marker, and their post-conditions assert exactly that: 1.4, 1.5, 1.6 and 1.13. Three others state the canonical stripping form. 1.14 promoted all eleven with the canonical form the Manager's close section 5.4 quotes. The four post-conditions are now false against the promoted files and need amending or the ruling needs reversing.

The declared file set is amended to exclude cr_scratch blocks whose target has been promoted, or the promotion's own first defect is a duplicate-id failure. MEASURED at 1.14: promotion took hard failures from 23 to 33; the eight new ones are exactly the eight blocks predicted (Q-BOOTSTRAP-PHASES, Q-DEGRADED-MODES, Q-BLOCKING-MODES, Q-STATE-FACTS, Q-STATE-ABNORMAL-READS, Q-STATE-CONSUMERS, Q-STATE-KEYS, Q-PAIR-IDENTICAL). tools/quantities.js --exclude-superseded implements the amendment and returns the count to 24. APPLIED AT R-4 as a clause of section 8, NOT as a flag. Ruling in the R-4 report section 3: a count that changes by nine depending on an unstated argument is an unruled number under section 3 rule 11, and a checker should not have a flag that makes its own verdict better. The escape hatch is inverted to --include-superseded.

tools/quantities.js exists as of 1.14, so CL-2 required its four rows to move to live. APPLIED AT R-2: CHK-14 to CHK-17 are live, which is possible only because AM-53 made their path cells paths in the same edit. CHK-23 is ruled the other way and does NOT move: its path named the authority (oracle/bootstrap_contract.md) rather than the artifact, and section 1 of the register says the register enumerates things that run. A contract does not run. The path becomes oracle/bootstrap_check.js, the executor sub-step 6.1 acquires, the contract moves into authority where it belongs, and the row stays specified because nothing runs it yet.

Add CHK-27 (tools/check_registers.js --manifest) and CHK-28 (--amendments). APPLIED AT R-2, both live and block: the script exits 1 on any FAIL line, measured, so block is the honest value and report would be false. Ids 27 and 28 leave 25 and 26 to AM-46, which stays owed: two specified rows for artifacts nobody has built are debt, not mechanism, and belong to the sub-step that builds them.

R4 confirmed by strict measurement at 1.14. APPLIED AT R-2 by AM-53 (the path cells) and AM-104 (CHK-27 and CHK-28 for tools/check_registers.js). CL-1 now covers all 10 files in the two scan roots with no uncovered file, verified by re-running the closure assertions over the amended register: 0 failures across CL-1 to CL-8.
